All values are read as strings. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package/blob/main/tinytab/_table.py#L250-L287){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Table.from_csv(path) ``` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [path]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Path]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The file to read. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The table read from the file. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Save a table with `Table.to_csv()`, then read it back. CSV files don't record types, so every value comes back as a string: ::: {#0aa0ff27 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import tempfile from pathlib import Path from tinytab import Table path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "menu.csv" Table({"item": ["coffee", "bagel"], "price": [3.5, 2.25]}).to_csv(path) Table.from_csv(path) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
itemprice
